title: Color palette + design-token consistency — every computed style
objective: Census every color, font, radius, shadow, and spacing value the site actually PAINTS, then find the off-palette one-offs, near-duplicate tokens, and component-class inconsistencies. Contrast re-verification rides along but the logged contrast items are known — this pass hunts NEW drift, not the recorded ratchets.

steps.do: Write _harness/audit10-stylecensus.js: for every public page + admin page at desktop-1440 and mobile-390, walk all rendered elements and collect computed {color, backgroundColor, borderColor, fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, lineHeight, borderRadius, boxShadow, letterSpacing} for every element that paints text or a visible box. Aggregate: value -> {count, pages, example selectors}. Output plans/audit10/state/stylecensus.json (committed). Dedupe rgb strings; ignore transparent/inherit noise.

Color analysis over the census: (a) cluster colors by Euclidean distance in sRGB; flag near-duplicates (distance < 12 but not identical) used in the same role — two almost-identical greys for the same border class is drift; (b) list every color used exactly once or twice site-wide with where — singletons are either deliberate accents or leaks; measure each singleton's element and judge; (c) map every painted color to its source: brand CSS var (--brand-*), Tailwind palette value, or hardcoded literal — hardcoded literals in brand-colored roles defeat the 4.23 repalette mechanism and are B-class (the site is owner-repaletteable; verify by injecting a test palette via the documented brand vars and screenshotting which elements DON'T follow).

The repalette drill (the one mutating test, browser-side only — no source edits): set the brand CSS variables to a contrasting test palette at runtime via page.addStyleTag on 5 representative pages; every element still painting the OLD brand blue/navy is a hardcode leak. Screenshot before/after into issues/. This reproduces nothing destructive and touches no files.

Typography scale: from the census, the set of {fontSize x fontWeight} pairs per component class. Flag: sizes used once (off-scale), heading levels whose visual size inverts their semantic level on any page, line-height outliers (<1.2 body text, >2 headings), and fontFamily values that are not the site stack (a raw 'sans-serif' or 'Times' leak).

Radii/shadows/borders: the site's component classes (cards, buttons, inputs, banners, figures) should each be internally consistent. From the census: every borderRadius value with its element classes — flag same-class drift (e.g. rounded-xl vs rounded-2xl on sibling cards); every boxShadow variant with usage — flag one-off shadows; border colors on the same background.

Contrast NEW-DRIFT check: run the existing brandtext + plan5c suites (do NOT rewrite the measurement — backdrop.js is the one implementation on purpose); confirm the failing set is byte-for-byte the logged set (brand-accent-on-dark-surfaces, count <= 13). Anything failing that is NOT in the logged set is a new finding. Then spot-measure (backdrop.js method) any element pass-1/2 flagged as looking low-contrast that the suites do not cover (admin pages are NOT covered by brandtext — measure the admin's grey-on-white label/help text yourself, AA 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large).

Dark-asset check: image assets containing baked-in text or brand color (logo variants, og-card, favicon svg, placeholder art) — consistent with the current palette? (Read the files; compare dominant colors against the brand vars.)

Record findings (hardcode leaks defeating repalette -> B; same-class token drift -> C; single-use near-duplicates -> batched D with instances[]), resolve pass-5 candidates, validate, ledger, commit 'audit10(pass-5): ...', push, delete mirror credential.

scope_fences: no repalette proposals, no 'better color' opinions — drift and leaks only
the logged contrast ratchets are not findings at any severity
admin visual bar is legible-and-operable (severity via that lens)
exit_criteria: stylecensus.json committed for all pages x 2 viewports
repalette drill screenshots captured with leak list
